To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the distribution of deeprooted woody species (i.e., groundwater-dependent vegetation) in southern Portugal was successfully modeled and that the results can be used to map the suitability to host this vegetation type in the region.

the distribution of deep rooted woody vegetation is mainly driven by climate and that the distribution of groundwater-dependent vegetation can be modeled using climate, hydrological and morphological variables, with a good agreement between model predictions and field data.

the distribution of groundwater-dependent vegetation (GDE) in a semi-aridal Mediterranean area is mainly driven by climate variables and that the relative proportion of the coefficients of the model predictor variables can be used as weighting factors to create a suitability model for GDE.
